message.content:
In this Go repository (github.com/usememos/memos, at /bench/home/work), the data layer is the `store` package (`/bench/home/work/store/*.go`), which defines persistent entity types like `store.User`, `store.Memo`, `store.Attachment`, `store.Reaction`, `store.MemoRelation`, `store.Webhook` (or `store.UserWebhook`), `store.IdentityProvider`, `store.Inbox`, `store.UserSetting`, `store.WorkspaceSetting`, `store.Activity`, `store.Shortcut`, etc.

First, list all top-level exported struct types defined directly in `store/*.go` (NOT in `store/db/*` subdirectories, NOT in `store/test/*`) that represent persistent entities (i.e., structs that map to database rows — typically things with an `ID` field or similar, used as return types from Get/List/Create functions). Use `grep -n "^type .* struct" store/*.go` to enumerate them.

Then, for each entity type, determine how many DISTINCT PACKAGES outside of `store` (and outside `store/db/*`) reference that type by name (e.g., `store.User`, `*store.Memo`, `[]*store.Attachment`, etc.) — count distinct package directories, not just files or occurrences. Relevant packages would include things like:
- `server/router/api/v1/*` (one package)
- `server/router/fileserver` (one package)
- `server/router/frontend` (if any)
- `server/auth` (one package)
- `server/runner/s3presign`, `server/runner/memopayload` (packages)
- `internal/*` subpackages if any reference store types
- `cmd/memos` (one package)
- `plugin/*` if it exists

For each candidate entity type (User, Memo, Attachment, Reaction, IdentityProvider, Webhook/UserWebhook, Inbox, UserSetting, WorkspaceSetting, Activity, Shortcut, MemoRelation, etc.), run something like:
`grep -rl "store\.User\b" --include=*.go /bench/home/work | grep -v "^/bench/home/work/store/" | xargs -n1 dirname | sort -u | wc -l`
(adjust the type name each time) to get a distinct-package count.

Report a ranked list of the top types by distinct package count (excluding the store package itself and its db subpackages), with the actual list of packages for the top 2-3 candidates so I can verify.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
All confirmed as distinct packages. Here's the full report.

## Entity structs defined in `store/*.go`

From `grep -n "^type .* struct" store/*.go`, filtering to the persistent-entity types (excluding `Find*`/`Update*`/`Delete*` query-option structs and the internal `Store`/`deploymentConfiguration` types):

- `User` (store/user.go)
- `Memo` (store/memo.go)
- `Attachment` (store/attachment.go)
- `Reaction` (store/reaction.go)
- `MemoRelation` (store/memo_relation.go)
- `Inbox` (store/inbox.go)
- `MemoShare` (store/memo_share.go)
- `UserSetting` (store/user_setting.go)
- `IdentityProvider` (store/idp.go)
- `UserIdentity` (store/user_identity.go)
- `InstanceSetting` (store/instance_setting.go)
- `AuthenticationConfigState` (store/auth_config.go)

Note: this repo has no `store/webhook.go`, `store/workspace_setting.go`, `store/activity.go`, or `store/shortcut.go` — those types (`Webhook`/`UserWebhook`, `WorkspaceSetting`, `Activity`, `Shortcut`) simply don't exist as entity structs in `store/*.go` in this codebase revision. (There is a `shortcut_service.go` under `server/router/api/v1`, but shortcuts aren't backed by a `store.Shortcut` struct — worth double-checking if you expected one.) Also note `InstanceSetting` is the workspace-level settings equivalent here (no separate `WorkspaceSetting` type).

One methodology note: the sample grep command `grep -v "^/bench/home/work/store/"` only strips lines with that literal absolute-path prefix. Since `grep -rl ... .` in this environment doesn't prepend `./` to paths, that filter actually let `store/db/mysql`, `store/db/postgres`, `store/db/sqlite`, and `store/test` leak into the "outside store" counts. I corrected this by filtering on `^store/` instead, which properly excludes all of `store/db/*` and `store/test` (both are `store`-internal). Counts below use the corrected filter.

## Ranked distinct-package counts (outside `store` and `store/db/*`)

| Rank | Type | Distinct packages |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `User` | 7 |
| 2 | `Memo` | 6 |
| 3 | `Attachment` | 4 |
| 4 (tie) | `MemoRelation` | 3 |
| 4 (tie) | `Inbox` | 3 |
| 4 (tie) | `MemoShare` | 3 |
| 7 | `UserIdentity` | 2 |
| 7 | `Reaction` | 2 |
| 9 | `UserSetting` | 1 |
| 9 | `IdentityProvider` | 1 |
| 9 | `InstanceSetting` | 1 |
| 12 | `AuthenticationConfigState` | 0 |

`cmd/memos` only calls `store.New(...)`, never references an entity type by name, and there is no `plugin/*` or `internal/*` package referencing `store` entity types at all.

## Package lists for the top 3 (verified, all distinct `package` declarations)

**`store.User` — 7 packages:**
- `server/auth` (package `auth`)
- `server/notification` (package `notification`)
- `server/router/api/v1` (package `v1`)
- `server/router/api/v1/test` (package `test`)
- `server/router/fileserver` (package `fileserver`)
- `server/router/frontend` (package `frontend`)
- `server/router/rss` (package `rss`)

**`store.Memo` — 6 packages:**
- `server/notification`
- `server/router/api/v1`
- `server/router/api/v1/test`
- `server/router/frontend`
- `server/router/rss`
- `server/runner/memopayload` (package `memopayload`)

**`store.Attachment` — 4 packages:**
- `server/router/api/v1`
- `server/router/api/v1/test`
- `server/router/fileserver`
- `server/router/rss`

`store.User` is the clear winner (referenced in auth context, notifications, the main v1 API service, its test package, the fileserver, the frontend router, and the RSS feed generator), followed by `store.Memo`, then `store.Attachment`. If you want `server/router/api/v1/test` excluded as "just tests," the ranking order is unchanged but User/Memo/Attachment/MemoShare/MemoRelation/Inbox each drop by 1.
